epic.title: compat(session): custom schemes, permission handlers, net stack, webRequest, session/profile and downloads over host-owned transport and KEL-135 profiles
epic.body:
## Scope
43 entities / 368 members: `Session` (88), `protocol` (18), `net`/`ClientRequest`/`IncomingMessage`/`WebSocket` (51), `DownloadItem` (28), `WebRequest`, `Cookies`, `ServiceWorkers`/`ServiceWorkerMain`, `Extensions`, `netLog`, 29 structures. Live today: no scheme registration (engine custom protocols are builder-time), no session/cookie/download/net facade, keld-guard evaluates `app.net.connect` URL scopes but nothing is wired to it, `web.camera`/`web.microphone` default-deny with a webview principal is live, KEL-135 gives one host-owned persistent profile per signed app (ephemeral in dev), KEL-79 (origin/resource transport) is Backlog with no spec file.

## Corpus demand
Zettlr `protocol.handle('safe-file')` (unprivileged scheme serving readable absolute paths; 23 consumers), `ses.clearStorageData` in 12 window factories, `net.online`; draw.io `session.defaultSession.webRequest.onHeadersReceived` (CSP for all contents) and `onBeforeRequest({urls:['file://*']})`, indirect `net.request` via electron-updater (`session.fromPartition('electron-updater')`); neither app installs a permission handler (Electron default-allow applies to them today); Extensions only in Zettlr's dev path.

## Maturity ladder
- L0: every entity exists with typed errors; never list published.
- L1: one live `Session` (= KEL-135 profile), `clearStorageData` subset, `net.fetch` over the Bun stack (legacy) / host net broker (strict), webRequest listeners as recorded no-ops behind host containment.
- L2: scheme table + `protocol.handle` producer routing, permission inversion, DownloadItem lifecycle pass pinned entries per engine.
- L3: Zettlr `safe-file://` workflow passes under `keld dev`.

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-79 (resource transport, parked), KEL-135 (profile identity; needs a `clear(types)` operation amendment), KEL-78 (strict net containment — decided: strict roles never connect directly), KEL-102 (broker admission), KEL-74/KEL-237 (evidence), arch 05 §2 resource adapter.

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters)
- Scheme declaration is static host configuration (`keld.config.ts` scheme table lifted by migrate from `registerSchemesAsPrivileged`), consumed by keld-wv at engine construction; `protocol.handle` registers a Bun producer behind the host resource adapter; bytes flow guard → broker; privilege bits are declared for migrate/scoreboard purposes but enforcement is per engine (WKWebView does not implement Electron's non-standard-scheme restrictions; custom schemes have no Service Workers on WKWebView).
- No permission handler ⇒ guard default-deny for the requesting webview principal (▲ against Electron auto-approve); an installed handler is consulted only after the guard allows and can only narrow; permission strings are engine-hook-dependent (a third column: guard-evaluable vs engine-decided).
- `net.*` wraps the Bun HTTP stack (never the engine session) under legacy; under strict it is a facade over a host net broker (new keld-native `net` row + spec; KEL-78 decides strict roles never connect directly). `useSessionCookies:true` is a typed ▲.
- `session.webRequest` is not emulated generically (only WebView2 could); listeners exist at L0 with typed errors, become recorded no-ops ▲ only after host file:// containment + always-on CSP injection land with a negative control (draw.io's two uses migrate via generated policy).
- v1 has exactly one `Session` = the KEL-135 profile; `fromPartition('persist:x')`, in-memory partitions, `fromPath` are typed ▲ until KEL-135 grows; `clearStorageData/clearCache` map to a KEL-135 host-side profile clear operation (not a new keld-native module).
- Never: Extensions/loadExtension, netLog, ServiceWorkerMain, network emulation, certificate verify overrides (legacy-profile question is owner-decided), proxy/connection control assigned explicitly.

refuter_verdicts_batch1.lens: Keld invariants, ownership and reuse: four uniques only; default-deny never bypassed or defaulted to allow; no Electron-isms in keld-core/keld-ipc; no parallel process model/transport/schema/parser/policy owner; reuse of existing owners (KEL-75/76/77/78/79/80/53/74/102/135/139-144); measured performance only; spec+Linear gate; prior decisions #312/#313/#319/#322/#323/#325 and KEL-127. Verified by reading the cited Keld files at origin/main d150a14; Electron/Apple/Microsoft receipts were not re-fetched and are judged only for consistency with Keld invariants.

verdicts.reason: The load-bearing atoms hold against the Keld sources: scheme declaration must be static and host-owned (keld-wv v0 omits register_scheme because engine custom protocols are builder-time; WKWebViewConfiguration/WebView2 environment constraints are receipted), and protocol.handle as a Bun producer behind the arch-05 adapter reuses the destination resource flow (engine → Rust adapter bound to active WebView+generation → keld-guard → broker → routed kipc to a supervised role) and the arch-02 keld://c/{channel} bulk lane rather than inventing a transport. Rejected alternatives (c) and (d) are correctly refused on one-owner and no-widening grounds. Prior decisions #322–#325 narrowed KEL-79 to product-spine subsets, but the KEL-139/KEL-142 specs contain no scheme or resource-transport text, so the author's 'parked, no spec file' blocker is accurate. Three corrections are required before this is specs-ready (see correction).
verdicts.evidence: <keld repo>/crates/keld-wv/src/engine.rs:8-11 ('post and register_scheme are omitted ... wry custom protocols are builder-time options'); engine.rs:59-64 NavTarget is only Html|Url (no scheme handler type exists); grep of crates/keld-wv/src for WKURLSchemeHandler/WebResourceRequested/register_uri_scheme returns nothing; <keld repo>/docs/architecture/05-webview-and-native.md:22-33 (destination trait has register_scheme(&str, SchemeHandler)), :150-210 (adapter→guard→broker→'Guarded routed kipc request with credit' to a Bun role; 'No direct Page-to-Bun socket'); <keld repo>/docs/architecture/02-ipc.md:271-274 ('Bulk therefore rides the custom scheme: keld://c/{channel} ... WKURLSchemeHandler / WebView2 WebResourceRequested / WebKitGTK 2.40+ streams'); <keld repo>/crates/keld-runtime/src/virtual_port.rs:15 MAX_PORT_MESSAGE_LEN = 4096 (confirms the 4096-byte inline port lane); <keld repo>/docs/specs/kel75-principalized-bun-child-roles.md:109-113 ('bounded inline kipc remains mandatory ... Any later bulk optimization needs a reproducible attributed end-to-end benchmark'); docs/research/library/execution-governance/229-execution-readiness-graph.md:146 and 236-execution-readiness-graph.md:228 (KEL-79/80 owner-parked); grep -i 'scheme|keld://|resource transport|KEL-79' over docs/specs/kel139-macos-product-spine.md and kel142-macos-renderer-bridge-api.md returns nothing.
verdicts.correction: (1) Privilege-bit placement and YAGNI: `bypassCSP` and `allowServiceWorkers` are hardening opt-outs, and architecture 03 §2 says CSP 'Opt-out is a named, linted grant' — they belong in the generated `keld.permissions.jsonc` (host-enforced), not in `keld.config.ts` (arch 04 §2 scopes that file to identity/windows/engine policy). Neither corpus app calls registerSchemesAsPrivileged, so a seven-bit privilege table has zero demand; v1 should carry scheme names only and record all privilege bits as ✘/▲ pending demand (root AGENTS.md YAGNI). (2) 'Any file bytes the handler reads go through the role's own fs.read grants' presumes the arch-05 §3 `fs+` 'strict-profile virtual Node-fs facade', which is not specced or live; under KEL-78 Zettlr's raw `fs.readFile` fails with an OS error, not KELD-GUARD001/002, so the stated test oracle is unreachable until that facade exists — add it to blocked_by. (3) The live fs broker caps one read at MAX_FS_CONTENT_BYTES = 8 MiB (crates/keld-native/src/fs.rs:42) with 64 KiB chunks; safe-file resources above 8 MiB would return the app's 500 where Electron returns 200 — either the resource broker path is a streaming/range path (arch 05 flow names 'range and bounded body') or this is a declared ▲.

verdicts.reason: The invariant atoms are confirmed by code and spec: keld-guard today denies every non-AppProcess principal before grant lookup (so a missing handler cannot become allow), the manifest parser ignores the `windows` top-level key (so `windows.<w>.web.*` grants are destination, consistent with the stated blocker), and KEL-102 §4 defines guard-before-handler and a webview policy-injection API whose destination row names 'Per-window grants, navigation rotation, origin context, channel grants and CSP'. 'Handler only narrows after guard Allow' is exactly the KEL-102 boundary. Two blockers are missing from the list (see correction).
verdicts.evidence: <keld repo>/crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs:699-706 (`if principal != Principal::AppProcess { return Decision::Deny(DenyReason::NotAppProcess { principal }); }` runs before grant lookup); lib.rs:564-571 ('Unknown top-level keys ($schema, windows, audit) are ignored. v0 evaluate reads app.<group>.<action>'); lib.rs:303-322 KELD-GUARD006/007 codes; <keld repo>/crates/keld-wv/src/media.rs:1-48 (guarded callback, 'Platform callbacks still do not pass an origin', 'A minted webview principal is still KELD-GUARD006 until window-level grants exist'); <keld repo>/docs/specs/kel102-host-guard-enforcement.md:423 ('### Webview policy-injection public API'), :515 ('### Guard-before-handler boundary'), :565 (destination row for the webview principal); <keld repo>/docs/architecture/03-security.md:242-262 (v0 media default-deny, 'saved browser permission preferences can bypass new-request callbacks'); docs/specs/kel135-persistent-profile-identity.md:654 ('KEL-79 owns origin/navigation').
verdicts.correction: Add two blockers: (a) `details.requestingUrl`/`isMainFrame` 'from host-minted navigation state' depends on origin/navigation ownership, which KEL-135:654 assigns to KEL-79 (parked) — without it the facade can only report the webview id, not an origin, and that must be a ▲. (b) The uniform rule 'guard default-deny for every permission string' is only enforceable for permission kinds the engine actually surfaces to the host; WKWebView exposes a media-capture decision handler but [inference, not verified here] no notifications or geolocation callback, WebView2 exposes a fixed PermissionKind enum, WebKitGTK exposes PermissionRequest subclasses. verdicts.reason: The enforcement location is NOT an open question: the approved KEL-78 strict-profile spec already decides it. decisions.question: How are Electron custom schemes (`protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged` + `protocol.handle`) realized when the scheme must exist before any engine view is created and the handler runs in a supervised Bun role?
decisions.proposed_answer: Scheme declaration is static, host-owned configuration (`keld.config.ts` scheme table with explicit privilege bits: standard/secure/supportFetchAPI/corsEnabled/allowServiceWorkers/stream/bypassCSP), consumed by keld-wv at engine construction on all three platforms; `keld migrate` lifts the app's `registerSchemesAsPrivileged` array into that table. `protocol.handle(scheme, handler)` is a facade that registers the Bun role as the producer for that scheme behind the architecture-05 host resource adapter: engine request → adapter binds active WebView+navigation generation → keld-guard evaluates the scheme/origin/method against the declared scheme and the producer role → routed kipc request to the Bun handler (Electron `Request`-shaped: url, method, headers, body, initiatorOrigin) → bounded `Response` chunks back through the adapter (WKURLSchemeHandler / WebResourceRequested / WebKitURISchemeRequest). Any file bytes the handler reads go through the role's own `fs.read` grants — the scheme itself mints no filesystem authority. Runtime `registerSchemesAsPrivileged` after `ready`, or for a scheme not in the static table, returns a typed KELD-COMPAT error; `protocol.handle` on a built-in scheme (file/http/https) is ✘ (see platform notes). Built-in intercept* and register*Protocol deprecated methods are facaded onto `handle` or ✘. [inference] This is the only shape that satisfies 'one host-owned scheme declaration' (research 186 row 1), the arch-05 guard-before-bytes flow, and the engine construction-time constraints.

decisions.question: Can `session.webRequest` (onBeforeRequest/onHeadersReceived/…) be emulated on system engines, and how do draw.io's two uses migrate?
decisions.proposed_answer: No generic emulation: WKWebView cannot intercept schemes it handles natively (http/https/file), WebKitGTK has no response-header rewrite hook for network loads, and only WebView2 (Chromium-derived) offers WebResourceRequested — a single-platform partial would be a silent per-OS divergence (forbidden). The quirks flag records the mapping so a later dynamic handler cannot silently widen it. WebRequest single-listener semantics ('Only the last attached listener will be used') are preserved in the L0 stub so re-registration behaves identically.
